transport.pagination: Exactly one urllib HTTP response per recorded call; no CLI/SDK paginator and no synthetic client NextToken.
transport.priorCapture: controls.json pagination already used signed-json-1.1; CLI aggregation did not explain its absent tokens.
transport.cliSupport: scripts/aws/aws_cli.py call/observe default paginate=True; callers must opt paginate=False. This probe bypasses CLI list calls entirely.

preliminaryCapture.note: Shared sibling eval globals caused prefix/name contamination before services. Calls preserve actual request IDs/prefixes; created empty cluster and task definition were cleaned in finally. Primary probe reruns in isolated closure. Preliminary envelope prefix is not authoritative for its request resource names.

documentation.promised: MaxResults between 1 and 50, default 50; up to MaxResults results and NextToken for another set; NextToken null when no more results; invalid token error documented HTTP 400.
MaxResults between 1 and 10, default 10; up to MaxResults results and NextToken for another set; omitted MaxResults returns up to 10 and NextToken if applicable.
MaxResults between 1 and 50, default 50; up to MaxResults results and NextToken for another set; NextToken null when no more results; invalid token error documented HTTP 400.

observations.contract: Explicit MaxResults=1 or 2 returned precisely 1 or 2 objects and omitted NextToken for all three list APIs, despite more owned matches. Repeated MaxResults=1 remained tokenless. Each call captured one raw signed HTTP response; this is not paginator aggregation.

With MaxResults omitted, DescribeScalingPolicies produced an opaque NextToken after 10 policies. For 12 policies on one target, the next request returned the remaining 2; this also occurred with PolicyTypes StepScaling. With explicit owned names spanning 4 targets and 15 policies, the first response held 10 and continuation held 5. Terminal responses omitted NextToken.

Replaying the same policy token succeeded HTTP 200 and returned the same 2 remaining policy names, but their order reversed relative to the first consumption. Stable iteration order is therefore not supported by this capture. Adding MaxResults=2 to the token request also succeeded and returned these same 2 names.

Keeping a token from ResourceId s0 but changing ResourceId to owned s1 returned InvalidNextTokenException HTTP 400. Adding PolicyNames selecting an owned policy belonging to s3 while keeping ResourceId s0 returned InternalServiceException with actually observed HTTP 500. The latter is one measured error, not a generalized filter-binding or validation contract.
For the token-producing policy API, invalid-token, empty-string, and truncated genuine token were all rejected with InvalidNextTokenException HTTP 400.

Deleting p0-11, an owned policy previously returned on the continuation page, then replaying the original token returned only p0-10 with HTTP 200. This case does not preserve a snapshot of the deleted record.

DescribeScalableTargets with 4 explicit owned IDs returned all 4 when MaxResults was omitted, without NextToken. DescribeScheduledActions returned 4 on the primary target, or 7 under explicit owned names across targets, with no NextToken when MaxResults was omitted. These populations do not cross the documented default 50 boundary.

limitations: Only AWS account 000000000000, us-east-1, ECS desired-count targets, and one isolated primary fixture were measured. Four targets, 15 step policies (12 on the primary target), and seven future schedules (four on primary) were created; no compute ran.

Real continuation was obtained only for DescribeScalingPolicies with MaxResults omitted. Token replay, altered page size/filter/resource, malformed tokens, and between-page deletion were exercised only for that API. No synthetic token was invented for targets or schedules.
Target/schedule populations did not exceed 50. Absence of tokens at explicit sizes 1/2 or below default-size populations does not establish that those APIs never paginate.

MaxResults=2 on an existing token was observed with exactly two records remaining; it establishes acceptance, not whether a smaller page size would produce another token. Captured genuine chains required only one continuation request.

Token expiry, cross-account/region use, cross-API reuse, insertion between pages, and deletion before a cursor position were not tested. Documentation does not promise token encoding, stable ordering, replay lifetime or snapshot consistency.
The observed HTTP 500 filter-change response is preserved verbatim; no inferred status or retry result is included.

The preliminary attempt encountered shared Eval state collision, created no services, and cleaned its empty cluster and task definition. Its separate chronological capture preserves actual inputs; main run used an isolated Python subprocess and create-response ownership guards. No temporary script file was created.

Task definitions were deregistered and deletion accepted; last DescribeTaskDefinition showed DELETE_IN_PROGRESS for both preliminary and primary attempts. Final tombstone disappearance was not observed. All services and clusters were observed INACTIVE, and targets/policies/schedules/alarms/task lists were observed empty.
productionImplications: resources.go pageLimit rejects every supplied NextToken and defaults to 50 for every list API. This is now demonstrably incomplete for DescribeScalingPolicies: native omitted-MaxResults pages default to 10 and yield valid consumable continuation when matching policies exceed 10.

Do not generalize previous controls.json tokenless MaxResults=1 observations into a universal no-continuation contract. Explicit MaxResults=1/2 still demonstrably truncate without tokens in this fixture, whereas omitted policy MaxResults produces tokens.

A future implementation should distinguish the measured policy default-page continuation path from explicit-limit observations. Tokens must be opaque to clients; this capture does not establish their native encoding or expiry.

No source changes are justified for target/schedule continuation from absence alone; their over-50 default boundary remains unmeasured. Retain a clearly scoped limitation rather than claim full AWS pagination parity.

Do not promise stable policy order or snapshot pagination; token replay reordered the same remaining names, and a deleted remaining policy disappeared. Treat the single filter-change internal error as evidence, not a desirable general production contract.
